items.description: South Devon coast from Start Point to Dawlish Warren
items.eaAreaName: Devon, Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly
items.message:
There is no longer a threat of flooding, though standing water and debris may still remain.
Coastal conditions are expected to improve and no flooding is expected.  
We will continue to monitor the situation and will issue further alerts or warnings if necessary.  
Continue to take care on waterside roads and footpaths and don't put yourself in unnecessary danger.

High tides and forecast weather conditions over the next three days may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible from 18:15 to 20:45 on 25/11/2026.
Locations most affected will be coastal roads and footpaths on the North Sea coast from Bridlington to Barmston. Tides will remain high with on-shore winds for the next few days meaning coastal flooding will remain possible.
We are closely monitoring the situation .
Avoid beaches and coastal promenades, which may be flooded.  
This message will be updated by 9:00PM on Wednesday 25 November or as the situation changes.

We will continue to monitor the situation and will issue further alerts or warnings if necessary.  
Continue to take care on waterside roads and footpaths and don't put yourself in unnecessary danger.

High tides, strong winds and large waves over the next two days may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible Flooding is possible from 5:45pm to 7:45pm on Wednesday 25th November.
Locations most affected will be low lying land and roads near rivers or on the coast, with spray being seen on the seafront paths. Flood gates in the area will be closed by the Local Authority which will make access difficult. Please take notice of the Flood Sign at the top of South Beach Road. 

The detailed forecast is for a peak level at Kings Lynn of 3.8mAODN at 6:45pm, on Wednesday 25th November, Wind Force 6, Easterly.
We are closely monitoring the situation .
Avoid beaches and coastal promenades, which may be flooded.  
This message will be updated by 10:00AM on Thursday 26 November or as the situation changes.
